description: Idon Wuta (Eye of Fire), Kano, Nigeria. A 3D globe app: search any place on Earth, see real NASA fire detections from the last 24 h and get fire alerts near you. Our AI forecasts next month’s fire risk, the likely fire type and class (A-K), how to prevent it and what to do (call 112). At its core, machine learning merges 25 years of NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire data into one burning calendar, tested on years it never saw. Hausa/English. We welcome ML, web and design skills.
summary: NASA’s satellites see every fire, but the record is split: MODIS and VIIRS count fire differently, and warnings rarely reach farmers. Idon Wuta (“Eye of Fire” in Hausa) uses an AI model, tested on unseen years, to harmonize MODIS and VIIRS into one burning activity calendar (Northern Nigeria pilot), then warns people anywhere: live NASA fire alerts confirmed by two satellites, wind and smoke direction, fire-class guidance, emergency numbers and evidence reports. Real data only. Live at idon-wuta.onrender.com.
details:
WHAT DOES IDON WUTA DO?

Idon Wuta ("Eye of Fire" in Hausa) is a live web application that harmonizes NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire records into one consistent burning activity calendar, then turns it into early warnings and practical guidance for the people who live with fire every dry season: farmers, herders, emergency responders, land managers and scientists.

Live app: idon-wuta.onrender.com | Code: github.com/hanifcodes/idon-wuta

HOW DOES IT WORK?

1. Data: We download NASA FIRMS active-fire detections from every satellite: MODIS on Terra (since 2000) and Aqua (since 2002), and VIIRS on S-NPP (2012 to 2 November 2026), NOAA-20 (2018) and NOAA-21 (2023). We use both science-quality and near-real-time products. Low-confidence detections and NASA-labelled non-vegetation sources (volcanoes, gas flares, offshore platforms) are removed.

2. Harmonization (AI): Detections are counted on a grid of 0.25-degree squares (about 27 km) for each week. A gradient-boosting model (scikit-learn, Poisson loss) learns what VIIRS would have detected from what MODIS detected, using the satellite platform, the season, neighbouring squares and each square's own history. It is validated leave-one-year-out: trained on all years but one, tested on the year held back, repeated for every year. It is compared with simple baselines (raw MODIS, one global ratio, monthly ratios), and the app ships whichever method wins. In our pilot, raw MODIS counted about 80% fewer fires than VIIRS in the same squares and weeks.

3. Burning activity calendar (Northern Nigeria pilot): For any selected area or state, the deep view shows the weekly burning calendar; when the season starts, peaks and ends; long-term trends, tested for significance (Mann-Kendall with Sen's slope, corrected for multiple testing); how this season compares with normal; and a farmer planner: "Harvest and clear firebreaks before...".

4. Fire outlook: A second model estimates the chance of fire in each square over the next 4 weeks. It is scored against two simple rules ("the usual for these weeks" and "same as the last 4 weeks"), and whichever wins on held-out years is shown, labelled.

5. Live early warning, worldwide: A 3D globe (NASA GIBS imagery, live FIRMS fires every 10 minutes) works for any place you search. Each detection gets a "confirmed" badge when two different satellites see it within 2 km and 12 hours, and a strength rating compared with every fire on Earth that day. Users can watch a farm, village or school and get alerts when fire is detected nearby, with an optional phone alert through Telegram.

6. What to do: Each place also shows wind and smoke direction (Meteomatics), the likely fire class and the right extinguisher, emergency numbers for about 200 countries, and a printable NASA fire evidence report listing every detection near a farm, for insurers and lenders.

WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS?

- Saves lives and livelihoods: warnings reach farmers and herders before fire reaches their harvest or herd.

- Keeps NASA's record usable: NASA plans to end MODIS science data in 2027. Harmonization keeps two decades of MODIS fire history comparable with VIIRS.

- Gives responders and land managers the critical periods to plan patrols, firebreaks and burning rules.

- Gives scientists a consistent record with its validation published openly.

- Trustworthy: real data only. Model outputs are labelled as predictions, estimates are marked, and missing data is shown as missing, never filled in.

WHAT DO WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE?

To extend the harmonized calendar and outlook from the Northern Nigeria pilot to every country, using NASA FIRMS country data; to add burned-area damage reports; to send spoken alerts in Hausa and by SMS for farmers without smartphones; and to give fire services a shared dashboard. Our goal: when a NASA satellite sees a fire first, the people nearby see it too.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES AND SOFTWARE

- Languages: Python, JavaScript, HTML/CSS, PowerShell

- AI and data: scikit-learn (HistGradientBoosting), pandas, NumPy

- Web: MapLibre GL (3D globe), Leaflet (deep-view map), a Python web server, Render (hosting), GitHub

- NASA data: FIRMS API and 24-hour fire files; GIBS imagery (WMS/WMTS)

- Other data: Meteomatics Weather API (Space Apps Global Offer), OpenStreetMap Nominatim, EOX Sentinel-2 cloudless imagery

- Reference files: Microsoft Learn emergency-number table; fire-class guidance from NFPA 10 and OSHA

- Hardware: a Windows laptop. No special hardware needed.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS

- The harmonized calendar and farmer dates cover the Northern Nigeria pilot area. Live fires, alerts, weather and emergency numbers work worldwide.

- Satellites can miss small, short or cloud-covered fires, and a detection shows that fire happened, not who caused it.

- The fire outlook currently shows the seasonal baseline wherever the AI has not yet beaten it.

- The Hausa interface is a draft awaiting review by a native speaker.
